clue.text: Return of loud and corpulent little man is concerning women

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the string of pieces is read from its end

parts.note: f (forte) is the musical direction for loud
corpulent means fat
Sid is a short form of the man's name Sidney

explanation.surface: A short, stout fellow named Sid makes a noisy comeback that bothers the women around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' reverses F + FAT + SID as a whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the female side, so the adjective relates to women.

clue.text: Keep talking about sport — crushing bore?

indicators.note: something crushing another holds it squeezed in its grip, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to sport a garment is to wear it, i.e. don it
a bore is a borehole, a well sunk for water

explanation.surface: Someone who won't stop going on about sport is a crushing bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' and 'bore' look like nouns about a dull talker; they are the verb DON and a drilled WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on a subject is to keep returning to it in speech, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Unexpected delay — sit without jiggling around

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome is one rearranged from the usual, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A surprise hold-up: someone is told to sit still and stop fidgeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something steadily means doing it firmly and evenly, without wobbling or shaking.

clue.text: Persuasive chaps maybe getting maiden to enter a place of vice?

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a den is a haunt of vice, as in a den of iniquity
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Smooth-talking men lure a young woman into a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman; in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising men are paid persuaders; 'maybe' marks them as one example of persuasive chaps.

clue.text: Swiss hero entering wood mostly sees ahead

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece is placed inside the other
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for wood is dropped

parts.note: a forest is a wood
William Tell is the legendary Swiss hero who shot an apple from his son's head

explanation.surface: William Tell walks into the woods and gazes into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves FORES and 'entering' is the container signal; the Swiss hero is the legendary archer William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell is to predict, i.e. to see what lies ahead.

clue.text: Act as judge when there's problem at a higher level

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
up means at a higher level

explanation.surface: A judge steps in when trouble arises in a higher court.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge sums up at the end of a trial, reviewing the evidence for the jury.

clue.text: Athenian statesman with good parting words

parts.note: Solon was the lawgiver and statesman of ancient Athens

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek politician delivers a fine farewell speech.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is an informal goodbye, so it is literally words said on parting.

clue.text: One's right to get cross about bad governance

indicators.note: about means around, so the cross-breed's name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
One's gives I (one) plus IS, read as 'one is'

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry about poor government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is a noun: a mule, the horse-donkey hybrid. One's = I'S, i.e. IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Misrule is government done badly or unjustly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Former drug mixture

parts.note: past means former, as in past times
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug cocktail from the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: A paste is a soft mixture of a powder with liquid.

clue.text: Old-fashioned member of the family dies

parts.note: passé means out of date, old-fashioned
a son is a family member

explanation.surface: A fusty old relative dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is a gentle euphemism for to die.

clue.text: Feature of mountain visible in fair weather off and on

indicators.note: off and on means intermittently, so every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A mountain ridge comes into view now and again when the weather is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: An arête is a sharp ridge between two glacial valleys, a mountain landform.

clue.text: Philosophers said to be in the clouds

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: mists are low clouds
oral means spoken, said aloud rather than written

explanation.surface: Philosophers have their heads in the clouds, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like it signals a sound-alike; here it means spoken, ORAL, set 'in' MISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moralists are thinkers concerned with ethics, a kind of philosopher.

clue.text: Sultan's wickedness, imprisoning a boy

definitions.note: read as 'Sultan is', the 's being the link

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking up inside, so the outer word holds the others

parts.note: sin is wickedness
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A sultan's cruelty extends to locking up a young boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century sultan of Egypt and Syria who fought the Crusaders.

clue.text: Certain to follow fashion that's very different from dreadlocks!

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, so the word for certain is placed after the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in bon ton
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A sure-fire trend that is the opposite of dreadlocks.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for fashion is a crossword staple from 'bon ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaven crown of a monk's head, the near opposite of long matted locks.

clue.text: Crocodile becoming this would double in length

definitions.text: Crocodile becoming this would double in length

parts.words: Crocodile becoming this would double in length
parts.note: a crocodile here is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs; lined up one behind another the line doubles in length

explanation.surface: Crocodile becoming this would double in length
explanation.walkthrough: The reptile is a decoy: a British 'crocodile' is a two-by-two line of schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking one behind another, in a single line, halves the width and doubles the length of a paired column.

clue.text: Soldier, about to get aboard that ship

indicators.note: getting aboard means going inside a vessel, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a fighter is a soldier
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to board that vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo ship.

clue.text: Measure of heat needed in the absence of hot period

indicators.note: in the absence of means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a therm is a unit of heat used for gas billing
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A heat reading is needed when there is no hot spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a period of time, such as a school term or term of office.

clue.text: Broadcasters and the press, group that's upset referees

parts.note: the media are broadcasters and the press together

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for group is read upwards

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: Journalists and a disgruntled group pass judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to act as go-between in a dispute, as a referee does.

clue.text: Intellectual support given to receiver of emails

indicators.note: given to means handed to, so the support comes first and the receiver follows it

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
an inbox is where emails arrive

explanation.surface: Intellectual backing for an email account.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is an informal term for a very clever person.

clue.text: Nerve in narrow part of body

definitions.meaning: nerve in the sense of cheek, audacity
the part joining head to shoulders

explanation.surface: A nerve located in a thin part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck means brazen cheek, and it is also the slender part of the body below the head.

clue.text: Important as he is to them

parts.note: the letters h and e sit in the middle of the word them, flanked by t and m

explanation.surface: He matters to them a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Central means principal or key, as in a central figure.

clue.text: Play informally a feature in this seminar

parts.note: the run of letters s s e m inside the words this seminar is mess written backwards, so mess turned around features there

explanation.surface: Fooling about is a feature of this seminar.
explanation.walkthrough: SSEM, spanning 'thiS SEMinar', is MESS turned around: the answer, read as wordplay, describes the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To mess around is to fool about or play without seriousness.

clue.text: Peacekeepers dream about what they want combatants to become?

definitions.text: what they want combatants to become

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces are deployed by the United Nations

indicators.note: about means all around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers imagine fighters laying down their weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacekeepers seek to disarm fighters, so the goal state is having no weapons.

clue.text: Series of prayers fired up some

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired up
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Some people are fired up by a run of prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of petitions in church worship, recited with responses.

clue.text: Bird featured in decorations

definitions.meaning: festive flags and streamers hung up for celebrations

explanation.surface: A bird appears among the festive decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunting is a family of seed-eating birds and also the strings of small flags hung for festivities.

clue.text: Hat that's not got left in country cottage

indicators.note: a hat that has not got something lacks it, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a bowler is a round hard felt hat

explanation.surface: A hat left behind in a country cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bower is a poetic word for a rustic dwelling or shady retreat.

clue.text: Area's cultivated to accommodate very good shrub

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in and house, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
cultivated soil is worked and turned over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means very good in crosswords

explanation.surface: An area is planted up to make room for a fine bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' yields SRAEA and 'to accommodate' is the container signal; PI as very good comes from pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiraea is a flowering garden shrub of the rose family.

clue.text: About time, authorise bargain

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for authorise goes around the other piece

parts.note: to seal a deal is to authorise it formally

explanation.surface: It's about time someone signed off on a cheap deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is something bought very cheaply, a bargain.

clue.text: Customer expecting protection bellowed endlessly in Herts town

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened word goes within the town's name

parts.note: Ware is a town in Hertfordshire (Herts), an English county north of London

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ranted means shouted angrily, bellowed

explanation.surface: A customer wanting security shouts himself hoarse in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims RANTED to RANTE, which goes 'in' WARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrantee is the person to whom a warranty or guarantee is given.

clue.text: Old boy about to get Palace's recognition? That's sweet

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the old boy's letters are reversed

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
an MBE is an honour conferred at Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: An old boy is about to be honoured by the Palace, and he's delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: MBE is Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a dome-shaped frozen dessert.

clue.text: Right person to give support in meeting

parts.note: an ally is someone who backs you

explanation.surface: The right person to back you up at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a mass gathering, as in a political rally.

clue.text: Cross, taken in by dealer? The reverse — not bothered

indicators.note: taken in means enclosed, so the cross goes inside the other piece
the reverse tells us to read the word dealer backwards

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A trader cheats someone who gets angry, but then shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' turns DEALER into RELAED, and X goes inside. It looks like a swap of container and contents but simply reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed means calm and unconcerned, i.e. untroubled.
